diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Moreover, we say that \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}} \in \Bll\) is resolved in direction \(k\) if \(
		\sideconfig_{\boldvec{i}, k} \subseteq \Bll.
	\)

Then, there must be some \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}} \in \sideconfig_{\boldvec{i}, k}\) that
	is problematic with \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{j}}\), and \(\abs{t_k - j_k} < \abs{i_k - j_k}\).

issues.failure_explanation: Resolvedness only says that the available neighbors in direction k belong to Bll. If i_k=j_k, every such neighbor has |t_k-j_k|=1 while |i_k-j_k|=0, so the asserted strict inequality is impossible. Problematic pairs with i_k=j_k are not excluded: they can lack the required straight chain in the other direction while i is resolved in direction k.

failure_location.quote:
Since \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}}\) is resolved in direction \(k\), by definition there exists
	\(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}}\in \sideconfig_{\boldvec{i},k}\) such that \(\abs{t_k - j_k} <
	\abs{i_k - j_k}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and propagate a condition ensuring i_k differs from j_k whenever the lemma is applied, and supply a separate argument for the equal-coordinate cases in the problematic-chain and algorithm proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the problematic-chain reduction, and hence the justification for reducing recursive checks in the exact-mesh algorithm, is unsupported in the equal-coordinate case.
issues.title: Resolved direction need not contain a neighbor closer to the other spline
issues.why_classification: The repair is localized but requires a genuine additional case argument and changes when the pruning lemma may be used.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\Require \(\thbbasis^{\boldvec{0}}_{L}\), a set of marked elements to refine per
		level \var{marked\_els}

issues.failure_explanation: The input contract does not require the initial hierarchical basis to be exact, but the initialization discards every pair whose two supports avoid the newly marked elements. A pre-existing problematic pair away from the marked region is therefore never checked; with empty or disjoint markings the algorithm can return the same inexact basis.

failure_location.quote:
\Ensure Updated truncated hierarchical basis \(\thbbasis^{\boldvec{0}}_{L}\) with no
		problematic intersections

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either require and use an initially exact basis, proving that only pairs incident to newly marked regions can become problematic, or retain all potentially problematic pairs in the initial check.
issues.overall_effect: The unconditional output guarantee and the formal claim that the algorithm always produces an exact mesh are false for the stated inputs.
issues.title: Exact-mesh algorithm can ignore pre-existing problematic pairs
issues.why_classification: A contained contract change or broader initial scan can preserve the method, but the current unconditional guarantee must be weakened or the checking procedure materially expanded.

issues.failure_explanation: The variable unchecked_funcs is initialized only inside initiate_unchecked_pairs, which returns only unchecked_pairs. It is never initialized or returned in alg:exact-mesh before being read and updated, so the main procedure is not executable as written. Moreover, its intended contents matter because they determine all pairs checked after adding an L-chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the intended unchecked_funcs state in alg:exact-mesh, return it from the initialization routine if appropriate, and prove that the resulting combinations include every new pair that can be problematic.
issues.overall_effect: The recursive rechecking stage is ill-defined, so neither termination nor removal of newly introduced problematic pairs is established.
issues.title: Main algorithm uses an undefined unchecked-function set
issues.why_classification: Initialization alone is local, but a complete repair must also establish the nontrivial coverage invariant for the chosen set of functions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We assume that \(\domain_{\level+1}\) is given as the union of
	supports of B-splines in \(\bspbasis_\level^{\boldvec{0}}\), that is \[
		\domain_{\level+1} \coloneqq \bigcup_{\bsp \in
		\tilde{\bspbasis}^{\boldvec{0}}_\level}\overline{\supp(\bsp)},\ \level = \{0,\dots,L-1\},
    \]

\Require 	
        \(\thbbasis^{\boldvec{0}}_{L}\),
        hierarchical level \(\level\),
        set of marked elements to refine per level \var{marked\_els}
Then the hierarchical complex \eqref{eq:hierarchical-complex} is exact for \(\level = 0, \ldots, L\).

issues.failure_explanation: The exactness theory is developed under the hypothesis that each refinement domain is a union of closed supports of level-l zero-form B-splines. The algorithm instead unions an arbitrary set of marked mesh elements directly into the domain. Such a union need not be a union of those supports, so the structural hypothesis needed by the chain arguments and the cited exactness theorem is not maintained.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each marked-element update by a specified support-closure operation producing a domain satisfying assum:refinement-domains, then redo the pair updates for every spline added by that closure.
issues.overall_effect: For the stated element-marking inputs, the algorithm's output can lie outside the regime covered by the exactness theorem, making its exactness guarantee unsupported even if all detected pairs are repaired.
issues.title: Element-based domain update does not preserve the required support-union hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The architecture can remain support-based, but the repair requires a nontrivial closure construction and corresponding rechecking rather than a purely notational correction.
